business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Procurement of Battery-Grade Lithium Carbonate Powder

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European legal system, with public registry and notarial mandatory formalities)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the European Union and Mexico on the protection of investments (in force since 2018, replacing EU Member State BITs, applied provisionally to Spain)
EU-Chile Association Agreement / EU-Chile Interim Trade Agreement (investment and trade provisions, applied to Spain)
Spain-Mexico BIT (signed 1995, in force 1997, largely superseded by EU-Mexico Agreement)
Spain-Argentina Double Taxation Agreement (DTA) (signed 1992, in force 1994)
EU-MERCOSUR Association Agreement (negotiated and agreed in principle, pending ratification; relevant for Argentina and Mercosur supply chains)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (as amended by Ley 11/2021 de 9 de julio and Real Decreto-Ley 7/2021); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, regulating the AML framework; Reglamento (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD) and Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (new AML package, phased application); Real Decreto 609/2023, de 11 de julio, creating the Central Registry of Beneficial Ownership (Realidad de Titularidades Reales) connecting corporate and financial information; Real Decreto 95/2024 (adapting Spanish law to the Single Digital Window for incorporation formalities); orden EHA/2963/2008 on the reporting of UBO by financial intermediaries; Ley 6/2023 (Securities and Investment Services Law) for relevant financial-sector interfaces.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or equivalent corporate existence document (foreign corporate shareholder or UBO entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry / Commercial Register in the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Modified/Updated Certificate of Good Standing or Extract of the Register of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of the UBO entity’s jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Legalized Power of Attorney (general or special) issued by each director/incorporator in favor of the Spanish incorporation agent or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the foreign jurisdiction or Spanish consular office abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; if executed in Spain, Spanish notarial deed required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passport/NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) of all directors, attorneys-in-fact, and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police authority, consular post, or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification plus, where registration or bank policy requires, apostille of signature or identity certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of funds certificate for the subscribers of capital (covering the capital contribution and any advance for pre-incorporation expenses)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution of the subscriber, often a bank in Spain or Latin American jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial/certified signature of bank officer or SWIFT-validated bank letter; not generally apostilled unless the Registrar expressly requests

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration (declaración de titularidad real) signed by each shareholder, identifying every natural-person UBO and the percentage of ownership/control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary (incorporated into the public deed of incorporation) and subsequently registered in the Registro de Titularidades Reales
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Part of the notarial minutes; no separate apostille is needed because it is incorporated into the original Spanish public deed

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against: (i) national Spanish lists, including the articles of Ley 10/2010 and its implementing regulations concerning politically exposed persons (PEPs), (ii) the European Union’s consolidated financial sanctions list (FINSAN), including anti-terrorist and asset-freeze regimes, (iii) the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists (ISIL/Al-Qaida and other sanctions regimes), (iv) the Spanish Ministry of Economy and Digital Transformation and the SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias) indicators, and (v) OFAC SDN List screening in accordance with international banking practice in the context of €/USD wire transfers and correspondent banking. Enhanced due diligence is required for any prospective member with ties to high-risk third countries, PEP status, or inconsistent source of funds. The SL must adopt and apply a risk-based CDD policy at incorporation, including verification of identity and UBO structure, ongoing monitoring, and record-keeping obligations where the SL falls within the scope of subject obliged entities under Article 2 of Ley 10/2010 if it engages in cross-border intermediate payments or third-party funding. For this procurement entity, which is a merchant/procurement company not itself a financial institution, compulsory AML measures apply primarily through banks and notaries, but the company’s internal compliance protocols should nonetheless mirror the statutory PEP and sanctions screening standards to avoid banking rejection and administrative liability.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (BORME and online name certification service: 'Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social' available through the Registro Mercantil Central electronic office, https://www.registradores.org/ and https://www.rmc.es/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be primarily in Spanish, using the Roman alphabet with correct Spanish orthography. Non-Spanish European Union official languages and Latin American Spanish variants are generally tolerated under EU principles of freedom of establishment; however, the use of English or non-Latin script (including Chinese) is permitted only if the name is transliterated/transcribed into Latin characters and does not jeopardize identifiability in the Mercantile Registry. For composite names mixing English terms, the registry requires that the name be sufficiently linked to the corporate object; otherwise it may demand a Spanish version for registered legal-security reasons.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tokens that are identical or phonetically too similar to an already-existing Spanish company name or trademark registry entry
Terms contrary to public order or infringing fundamental rights
Names incorrectly implying public-sector linkage, government sponsorship, royal patronage, or official EU status
Terms that mislead the public regarding the corporate form (e.g., cannot use 'S.A.' if incorporating S.L., cannot use 'S.A.' or 'S.L.' prematurely)

Prohibited regulated-activity terms requiring prior governmental authorization, such as 'Banco', 'Seguros', 'Fondo de Inversión', 'Sociedad de Valores', 'Aseguradora', 'Minería' if a mining concession is absent, 'Financiera', 'Arbitraje' (unless licensed or authorized by supervisory ministries)
Terms containing 'España' or 'Nacional' without prior administrative authorization

Misleading references to geographic origins, especially 'Andina', 'Patagonia', 'Latinoamérica', or foreign country names (e.g., 'Argentina', 'México', 'Chile') if such use is not genuinely justified by the corporate object, and in all cases, the registry requires that the name be distinctive rather than purely descriptive
Tokens containing 'Litio', 'Lithium', 'Carbonate', 'Battery' when combined with regulated catchwords implying an industrial/extractive license or mineral reserve concession not yet held by the SL
Denominations suggesting non-profit status or misleading public character, such as 'Fundación', 'Cooperativa', 'Asociación' without corresponding legal form
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event the Central Mercantile Registry rejects a requested name, the incorporator or its legal representative may, within fifteen (15) business days from notification, file a written appeal (escrito de recurso) addressed to the Central Mercantile Registry Director (Registro Mercantil Central) pursuant to Articles 403-404 of the Spanish Companies Act (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio). The appeal must set out the grounds for novelty, identifiability, and lawfulness. The Registry must decide within one month; failure to decide is deemed grounds for a formal complaint before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) (formerly DGRN). The Registry may reject the requested name due to phonetic/graphic identity with an existing name, inclusion of prohibited terms, or objectionable content. If the appeal is denied, a new name application may be filed; the applicant may alternatively request a name certificate for a secondary alternative name once the prior certificate is revoked. The name reservation window is the statutory term of 30 days from issuance of the negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación), after which the reservation lapses and a new request is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible in practice for initial incorporation subject to strict compliance with Article 9 of the Spanish Companies Act (registered office must be the location of actual management or main establishment). For a cross-border battery-metals arbitrage/procurement company that is not subject to specific local physical-presence licensing, a 'virtual office' or registered-agent address may be accepted by the Mercantile Registry and banks only where the administrative seat, correspondence management, and accounting records are genuinely monitored from a real Spanish address. Mere zero-footprint virtual offices are increasingly rejected by Spanish notaries and banks. For this industry (wholesale procurement and trade), a formally designated Spanish registered office, even if served by a third-party office provider, is admissible provided there is: (i) a contractual office-use or domiciliation agreement, (ii) actual personnel or an accountable director resident in Spain, and (iii) access to the records by the registry, AEAT (tax agency), and SEPBLAC. The transaction-level economic substance must be verifiable through Spanish bank accounts, commercial invoices, and warehouse/distribution arrangements when the company's business model involves imports from Latin America into the EU.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections: 15-25% during the first fiscal year for a high-risk procurement and foreign-supply-chain industry, especially if the Spanish registered office is a virtual/domiciliation address. The AEAT and SEPBLAC may conduct unannounced inspections, typically in cases of: volume of intra-EU/third-country invoicing disproportionate to the declared workforce, frequent use of cash or high-value wire transfer transactions with Latin American jurisdictions, or anomalies in VAT registration (NIF-UE) filings. For an SL engaged in ISIC 4662 wholesale procurement of battery-grade lithium carbonate, with cross-border arbitrage and significant movement of funds, the likelihood of a documentary or physical-challenge inspection is elevated to 25-35% if the company applies for VAT refunds, uses third-country intermediaries, or reports a low fixed-asset base with high revenue.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for certified Spanish translation of ISIC/NAICS-based corporate objects and shareholder resolutions (EUR 250-450)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and UBO piercing review of shareholders and Latin American counterparty supply-chain structure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish corporate law firm / cross-border due diligence counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for cross-border UBO and sanctions due diligence (EUR 1,500-2,500 fixed or hourly)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of the deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) including UBO declarations and JOA/Board powers

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory Notary Tariff (Arancel Notarial) established by Royal Decree 1426/1989, as amended; fees depend on the notary’s territorial colegio and document extension, typical range EUR 600-1,100

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing fee for provisional registration of the company in the Mercantile Registry (inscripción provisional in the Registro Mercantil Provincial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) where the registered office is located
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff published by the Colegio de Registradores; SL with standard capital and deed pages typically EUR 150-220

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation notice in BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: BORME, Agencia Estatal Boletín Oficial del Estado (Spanish Official Gazette) / Registro Mercantil Central
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication fee, approximately EUR 40-80 per alert/excerpt based on text length

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille fees for foreign corporate documents of ultimate parent / UBO (Mexico, Argentina, Chile or other Latin American source) including translator and authentication of signatures
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign Ministry/Consular Offices in the country of issuance and Spanish consulate where apostille is not available
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local and international consular tariffs; per-document apostille fees plus legalization administrative costs (Latin American sources vary USD 40-120 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation of apostilled foreign UBO documents, financial references, and sanctions/PEP screening records
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market per-page certified translation rate (approximately EUR 0.10-0.30/word or EUR 45-80/page; complex corporate documents 10-30 pages)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE application and processing for non-resident directors/shareholders, if applicable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee for NIE (EU: EUR 10-30 depending on issuance by consulate vs. in-country police)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization / Hague Apostille of bank reference and corporate authorization for opening the company's Spanish bank account (or compliance service if account opening accompanies formation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Contingency buffer of 10-20% of translation/certification fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (articles 20-34 on incorporation, 21 capital mínimum, 58-107 on articles and administration categories)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office domicile; name reservation through Registro Mercantil Central; notarial filings before a Spanish Notary
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (public deed of incorporation) filed for inscription in the Registro Mercantil Provincial
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 3,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and paid in at subscription, evidenced by a Spanish bank deposit certificate (certificado bancario de ingreso) or cash paid to the notary; capital must be maintained, and if less than statutory limits when losses reduce net worth, mandatory dissolution rules apply
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [SL NAME]. The shareholders having executed the incorporation deed on [date], the Directors unanimously resolve: (1) to accept ownership of the entire subscribed share capital of EUR [amount] paid in by the shareholders; (2) to adopt as the corporate domicile the office located at [address], within the jurisdiction of the Registro Mercantil of [province]; (3) to appoint [Name] as Sole Managing Director, [Name] as Chairman, and [Name] as Secretary, each accepting office; (4) to authorize the Managing Director and Secretary to execute all filings, registrations, and third-party formalities arising from this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the corporate name with the Registro Mercantil Central
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (online certification application through the Spanish Ministry of Justice portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a nombre (negative name certification) request with three alternative corporate name options. The certification must be obtained before signing the incorporation deed and is valid for three months. Complete the form electronically, pay the regulated fee, and obtain a negative certification confirming proposals of the merging entity, mergers, name changes or adoptions. Attach the certificate to the notary instruction.
required_dossiers: Application form for name certification (modelo de solicitud de certificación negativa)
Identification documents of all founding shareholders (passport/NIE)
Proposed corporate name and activity-related description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certification is negative because names are identical or confusable with an existing company, refile immediately with revised alternatives. If the certificate expires, request a new certificate. If the registry refuses for lacking signatures, rectify the power of attorney or notarial certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a bank account and deposit the minimum capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banking entity in Spain authorized for escrow deposits (accounts in Spanish entities supervised by Banco de España)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional 'sociedad en formación' account in the name of the proposed SL and deposit the minimum capital (EUR 3,000 or higher if required by articles). Request a deposit certificate (certificación bancaria de saldo y retención) from the bank stating that the funds are available and blocked until the public deed is executed. The bank certificate is presented to the notary and the funds remain blocked.
required_dossiers: NIE or passport of each founding partner
Draft incorporation deed
Proof of reserved corporate name (negative name certificate)
Source of funds statement for AML/CFT compliance
Bank mandate for future corporate accounts (signed model)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses due to inadequate AML documentation, supplement with deposit accounts by the partner's rightful ownership, sign a SWIFT/transfer trace, or open the account at another bank. If the bank does not issue the certificate in time, amend the deed deed timetable and then obtain the certificate. A bank refusal is not final; the entity may use a notary's deputy account where legally permissible.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the incorporation deed before a Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the district of the registered office (Colegio Notarial de la circunscripción)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the notary, each shareholder subscribes to the shares, approves the bylaws (estatutos), appoints the administration organ, and consents to the deed. Verify the identity of the incorporators, their representation, the reserved name certificate, the bank deposit certificate, and the capital. Sign the deed and all duplicate executions and authorize the deed. The notary will withhold and later send the first copy for registration.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate from the Registro Mercantil Central
Certificate of bank deposit for the capital (or notarial signature of payment by bank check or cash if lawfully allowed)
Notarized identification of founders (passport/NIE) and any powers of attorney
Signed draft articles of association (estatutos sociales)
Tax identification number (NIF) of each founder if already obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary observes deficiencies (e.g. missing certificate, incorrect statutory clauses, unlawful article), correct the draft and re-execute the deed. If a founding partner fails to attend, obtain a valid special power of attorney (poder especial) for the deed or receive a ratification before the same notary. Notarial refusal must be reasoned; if not, the next notary can accept the same instruction after remedying the cause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the provisional NIF and file the individual tax declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria (the Spanish Tax Agency) — Subdirección General de Gestión Tributaria
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the month of deed execution, apply for the provisional NIF (CIF) of the corporation on form Modelo 030. Payment of the Spanish capital tax (Impuesto de Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados, EPJD) is declared via Modelo 600 in the corresponding tax office. Hold the provisional NIF until final inscription; thereafter request definitive NIF. Also complete the census declaration (Modelo 036).
required_dossiers: Copy of the notarial incorporation deed (primera copia)
Modelo 030 for provisional NIF application
Modelo 600 for the EPJD/AJD capital tax
Modelo 036/036 and general documentation for the census registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Agency rejects the NIF application due to discrepancies between the deed and copy, correct the data and resubmit. If the NIF is issued as 'borrador' pending registration, use the provisional NIF for interim acts and request the final one after registration. For Modelo 600, if the tax office disagrees on the taxable basis file a alegación with the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the deed for commercial registration in the Registro Mercantil Provincial
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first copy of the deed, a Notarial Record, the completed Modelo 600 with payment evidence, and the application for inscription. The registry examines legal and substantive privity, verifying the legal formation procedure. After qualification, the registry enters the SL into the commercial registry, later returning the registered deed with the inscription certificate. The final NIF is then issued.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed of incorporation
Notarial record of legalization of corporate books, if applicable at this stage
Modelo 600 duly paid (AJ duty)
Application for registration signed by the administrators
Power of attorney of the representative filing (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a suspension agreement or denial ('calificación negativa'), the documentation must be corrected and the defect repaired, or an appeal may be filed in legal proceedings. Remediation typically consists of amending the deed by obtaining a new notarial deed of rectification. Registry suspension notices must be reviewed and followed; if no deficiency is remedied within a reasonable period, the registry may refuse registration and the deed becomes subject to expiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalize corporate books and finalize institutional registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (once the SL is registered); Registro Mercantil Central for cross-border filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, present the statutory corporate books (shareholder register, minutes book, inventory/balance book, partible book) for legalization at the Registry. Attend administrative tax registration (census, IVA, employment) and obtain the definitive NIF. For storage or office premises, submit a municipal 'comunicación previa' or 'licencia de actividad' before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate of the SL issued by the Registro Mercantil
Statutory books (Libro de Registro de Socios, Libro de Actas, Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)
Form 036/036 final census declaration
Notarial legalization certificate of books, if previously required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry refuses to legalize books because the SL is not yet fully registered, wait until the registration is effective; then resubmit. If books contain defects, modify and replace before presentation. For municipality, if the notice is challenged or additional licenses are required, submit the necessary environmental or building documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — pure wholesale distribution of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder (ISIC 4662). No industrial establishment, manufacturing, or hazardous process authorization is required under Spanish industrial law; if a storage or battery blending plant is later set up, the Consejería competente en industria y energía of the Autonomous Community would become competent.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable for the simply commercial cross-border procurement and wholesale distribution activity. Should a warehouse be deployed, the relevant title is 'licencia urbanística/ambiental de actividad' or 'comunicación previa' under municipal law, and for stabilization or mixing operations an 'autorización ambiental integrada' could apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico and regional authorities (Autonomic Consejerías de Medio Ambiente)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for pure wholesale trade without physical transformation. If surface storage of chemical products exceeds Annex II thresholds (e.g., hazardous substances due to lithium carbonate dust), the corresponding autonomous EIA screening ('evaluación de impacto ambiental simplificada') may become compulsory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not affected if no wastewater or air emissions. In the case of future storage: compliance with Real Decreto 115/2017 (REACH/CLP), sectorial emission values under Ley 7/2022 (circular economy and waste), and, if applicable, atmospheric emissions limits for particulate matter (e.g., 10 mg/Nm3 for PM) and dust control under Real Decreto 430/2004; waste handling under Real Decreto 833/1988 and the waste producer registry rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under Código Técnico de la Edificación (CTE DB-SI) and Real Decreto 2267/2004 (industrial fire facilities) only if premises are used. Structural load inspection under municipal or regional building inspection agreements when changing use. Workplace clearance under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, with basic documentation of working conditions and a service of prevention prior to any employment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the AEAT Sede Electrónica and its Census of Entrepreneurs, Professionals and Withholding Agents. Customs matters are administered through the AEAT Department of Customs and Special Taxes. The competent regional authorities of the Basque Country and Navarra apply their own tax systems, but they are not applicable to an ordinary company tax resident in the common Spanish tax territory unless separately established there.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Spanish Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) from the AEAT. The normal procedure is: (1) reserve the corporate name and execute the incorporation deed before a Spanish notary; (2) apply for a provisional NIF using Form 036, generally through the notary or electronically by an authorized representative; (3) register the deed with the Commercial Registry; (4) submit the registered deed and permanent corporate documentation to the AEAT and obtain the definitive NIF; (5) register the business activity, tax address, directors, shareholders where required, and applicable tax obligations through Form 036; (6) request registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios (ROI) if intra-EU supplies or acquisitions require a Spanish VAT identification number; and (7) obtain the NIF-IVA, normally formatted as ES plus the Spanish NIF, after validation in the VIES system. A foreign company without a Spanish establishment or incorporation may request a Spanish NIF by filing Form 036 through its authorized representative, Spanish tax representative where legally required, or an accredited intermediary. Supporting documents generally include the foreign certificate of incorporation or equivalent registry extract, constitutional documents, proof of legal existence, identification of directors and beneficial owners where required, proof of authority of the representative, and certified Spanish translations and legalization or apostille where applicable. An EORI number must be obtained for customs import and export operations; the EORI is generally linked to the entity's EU tax identity and is administered through the Spanish customs authority. VAT registration is not based on a separate standalone VAT number: the Spanish NIF-IVA is the NIF with the ES prefix, subject to ROI registration where intra-EU transactions are involved.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no United States-style check-the-box election for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. An SL is a separate legal person and is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax on its worldwide income if tax resident in Spain. Available elections or regimes may include the optional special regime for tax consolidation within a qualifying group, the special regime for mergers, demergers, contributions of assets and exchanges of shares, and other statutory special regimes where eligibility conditions are satisfied. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch rules generally deny deductions or impose corresponding income inclusions for arrangements producing deduction/non-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes, subject to statutory conditions. These mechanisms do not convert an SL into a pass-through entity. Tax residence depends principally on incorporation, registered office, or effective management in Spain, subject to applicable tax treaties.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Spanish Value Added Tax (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, or IVA), harmonized with the EU VAT Directive. Spanish customs and import VAT rules also apply to goods entering the Spanish VAT territory. The Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla are outside the ordinary Spanish VAT territory and have separate indirect tax systems.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic turnover threshold applies for Spanish VAT registration. A person carrying on an economic activity is generally a taxable person from the commencement of the activity and must register before making taxable transactions, subject to specific rules for intra-EU transactions, imports, distance sales, and special schemes. Therefore, the effective statutory registration threshold is EUR 0. Registration is made through Form 036. Separate EU-wide thresholds and destination-country rules can apply to intra-EU distance sales and certain electronic or consumer supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for every domestic invoice. Invoices must comply with Spanish invoicing rules, including mandatory content, sequential numbering, authenticity, integrity, legibility, retention, and electronic-signature or equivalent controls where applicable. The Immediate Supply of Information system (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) requires qualifying taxpayers, including taxpayers registered in the monthly VAT refund regime, large enterprises meeting the statutory turnover threshold, and VAT groups, to transmit prescribed invoice-register data electronically to the AEAT, generally within four business days, subject to statutory exceptions and adjustments. The electronic invoicing framework under Law 18/2022 establishes broader B2B electronic invoicing obligations, but implementation depends on the applicable regulatory development and effective dates. The VERI*FACTU and related billing-system integrity rules introduce requirements for secure, traceable and tamper-resistant invoicing records and electronic reporting or verification features according to the taxpayer category and applicable implementation timetable. A company must also comply with electronic filing and electronic communications requirements when legally subject to them. These regimes should not be treated as a blanket real-time customs or VAT clearance mandate unless the specific taxpayer and transaction fall within SII, customs electronic declaration, or another designated reporting system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from the Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law, provided the statutory export conditions are met and the exporter retains reliable evidence that the goods left the EU customs territory. The exporter must be able to link the commercial invoice, transport, customs declaration, goods, buyer, and payment or contractual records. Supplies to customers established outside the EU do not automatically qualify if the goods remain in Spain or the EU. Intra-EU supplies are generally exempt with the right to deduct under separate rules and require valid customer VAT identification and transport evidence. Services supplied to business customers established outside Spain are generally governed by place-of-supply rules and may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT rather than technically zero-rated; the supplier must substantiate customer business status, location, and the absence of a Spanish fixed establishment receiving the service. Services directly connected with exports or international transport may qualify for specific exemptions if their statutory conditions are satisfied. Import VAT is not eliminated by later export unless the relevant customs and VAT procedures, such as customs warehousing, inward processing, or other suspension arrangements, are properly used.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration submitted through the Spanish customs system, normally containing the correct customs procedure, commodity classification, customs value, origin information where relevant, exporter and consignee data, and the Movement Reference Number (MRN).
Electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory, including the Export Accompanying Document or equivalent customs exit message and the exit results generated by the customs system.
Commercial invoice identifying the seller, buyer, goods description, quantity, price, delivery terms, currency, and export transaction reference.

Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, sea waybill, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or courier documentation, demonstrating movement of the identified goods to a non-EU destination.
Purchase order, sales contract, delivery terms, insurance records, warehouse release records, and logistics records sufficient to reconcile the goods with the export declaration.
Import or entry evidence from the destination country where available, particularly where Spanish customs exit evidence is incomplete or additional proof is needed.

Proof of payment or other commercial settlement records, including bank transfer records or letter-of-credit documentation, where relevant to corroborate the transaction. Inward remittance certification is not generally a Spanish statutory prerequisite for export VAT exemption.

Evidence supporting any export-related service exemption, including the underlying export declaration, transport contract, service invoice, and proof that the service is directly connected with the qualifying export or international movement.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days as a condition for applying the export VAT exemption. Foreign-exchange controls do not impose a general 180-day repatriation deadline for ordinary commercial exports. Failure to prove that goods left the EU, incorrect classification of an intra-EU or offshore service transaction, fictitious exports, falsified customs evidence, or unsupported input-VAT recovery can result in assessment of the VAT that should have been charged or repaid, late-payment interest, and recovery of improperly refunded VAT. Under the General Tax Law, sanctions for failure to pay or underpayment may generally range from 50% to 150% of the improperly unpaid amount depending on the seriousness, concealment, repeated conduct, and use of fraudulent means. Separate sanctions may apply to inaccurate tax returns, improper VAT invoices, bookkeeping failures, obstruction of inspection, and failure to retain supporting records. Fraudulent customs declarations may also trigger customs debt, customs administrative penalties, seizure or forfeiture consequences, and potentially criminal liability for tax or customs fraud. The AEAT may deny the exemption retrospectively and claw back input VAT where the taxpayer cannot establish the objective export conditions, the identity and movement of the goods, or the authenticity of the supporting documentation. Statutory limitation periods, generally four years for tax assessment and sanctioning actions subject to interruption rules, should be considered when retaining records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) under the remit of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation; foreign exchange policy is governed by EU capital movement liberalisation (Articles 63-66 TFEU) and Real Decreto 1027/2003, amended by Real Decreto 1492/2007, concerning statistical and administrative declarations of external transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions in the euro area. Spain imposes no exchange controls, no surrender or repatriation restrictions, and no prior authorisation for trade-related payments or profit remittances. Foreign residents may freely repatriate dividends, capital gains, and loan principal, provided that the underlying transactions meet the documentary and tax compliance standards. Only statistical reporting obligations apply, via the Banco de España R/A system (Declaración de Operaciones con el Exterior, N-1 form) for payments exceeding EUR 50,000, consolidated by the bank; direct reporting may be required for financial operations above EUR 1,000,000. No material convertibility hurdle exists for battery-grade lithium carbonate procurement; EUR/USD and EUR/CNY markets are deep and unrestricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Spain does not impose any statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. A Spanish SL may retain export receipts in foreign currency in its operational account or convert them into EUR at market rates without Banco de España approval. The only requirements are the standard anti-money laundering transaction record-keeping obligations under Ley 10/2010 and the statistical reporting threshold of EUR 50,000 per individual transaction or aggregated annual relationships.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Cuenta Operativa) plus optional Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Depósito de Capital)
Operational Account (Cuenta Operativa) plus trade finance and SWIFT LC lines
Operational Account (Cuenta Operativa) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account with selective corporate onboarding

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as primary treasury rail, Medium as supplementary liquidity tool. Spanish-registered or EU-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs) authorised under Real Decreto 778/2023 and the EU EMD2 framework can serve as ancillary accounts for FX conversions and operational payments, but they are inadequate as the main settlement account for this Deal because: (i) the AML risk tier (Medium Risk Enhanced) for wholesale lithium carbonate trading triggers enhanced due diligence that most EMIs reject; (ii) EMIs generally cannot issue or receive commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT707) or structured trade products; (iii) the capital escrow requirement for SL formation is only accepted by full credit institutions, not EMIs; and (iv) Banco de España supervisors expect a physical bank relationship for entities with an annual flow exceeding EUR 1 million. A hybrid structure — Tier 1 bank for settlement/LC and an EU EMI for spot FX convenience — is permissible but must be disclosed to the Tier 1 bank to avoid transaction-level red flags.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the de facto mandate for the SL administrator or an authorised representative holding a notarised and Apostilled power of attorney. Ley 10/2010 requires customer identification through physical presentation of original identity documents; for corporate entities, the administrator must sign the account opening mandate (Poder de Administración) before the bank's compliance officer. Remote onboarding through video identification (TrustID equivalent) is accepted by certain Tier 1 banks only for non-executive signatories holding a Spanish digital certificate, and only if the authorised representative appears in-branch. The mandatory in-person interview is the standard control measure for non-resident owned SLs and cannot be waived for the 'Medium Risk Enhanced' classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity when the SL is owned by non-EU shareholders or an offshore holding entity; the bank will demand the Titular Real / UBO register under Real Decreto 304/2014.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and Apostilled certificate of incorporation of the SL and each upstream entity; formal UBO declaration (form 03-01 of Banco de España); corporate registry abstract (certificación del Registro Mercantil); passport copies of all natural persons holding over 25%; tax residence certificates (Modelo 290/294 status) from all relevant jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-counterparty concentration in high-risk jurisdictions (China, Chile, Argentina, or offshore free-trade zones) for battery-grade lithium carbonate imports causing the transaction-flow risk engine to produce alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed supply agreements with Incoterms 2020 clauses; pro-forma invoices and final commercial invoices; LLI / ITS weight certificates and independent SGS or Bureau Veritas assay reports; SWIFT MT103 payment history; bank reference letters from the counterparty's correspondent bank; corporate registry evidence of the supplier's manufacturing capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from a non-Spanish private bank or family trust creates a mismatch between the declared business plan and the expected contribution amount.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of funds dossier: 12-month audited bank statements, foreign exchange transaction confirmation slips, source-of-wealth declaration for all UBOs, notarised shareholder loan agreements (if applicable), and a signed letter explaining the economic substance of the lithium arbitrage model with a 3-year financial forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the SL's declared annual turnover expectation (EUR 5M+ commodity flow) and its modest share capital cause rejection at the credit committee stage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan audited by an independent Spanish economic-financial advisor; signed contracts with anchor buyers or off-takers; warehouse lease agreements or logistics provider contracts in Spain (or EU ports); evidence of credit insurance or trade credit lines with COFACE or CESCE covering the receivable portfolio.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For formation of the ES_SL entity, capital must be wired from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the notary-designated provisional escrow account (Cuenta de Depósito de Capital) held at a Spanish Tier 1 credit institution. The wire must comply with SEPA or SWIFT standards; for non-EUR transfers the funds are converted upon landing and a Certificado Bancario de Saldo is issued by the bank for the notary deed (escritura). The correct SWIFT purpose code or clearing descriptor must be stated as 'Capital Contribution / Desembolso de Capital Social'; the bank files the N-1 external-transaction declaration with Banco de España where the deposit exceeds EUR 50,000. Incoming funds from Latin American jurisdictions should be accompanied by the sender's source-of-funds certificate and copy of the wire instruction with the corresponding DEA/No. de aviso to satisfy the enhanced due diligence protocol of Ley 10/2010. Post-registration, the operator may transfer the issued capital from the escrow into the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for battery-grade lithium carbonate will be executed through two preferred rails: (i) direct SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic transfer against invoice, using SPF (single payment) under payment terms of 30% advance / 70% against BL, or (ii) an irrevocable commercial Letter of Credit opened via the Spanish Tier 1 bank's trade finance desk using SWIFT MT700/MT707 governed by UCP 600, payable at sight to the advising and confirming bank (typically the supplier's bank in Chile, China, or Australia). For large cargoes exceeding EUR 1 million, the documentary LC is the recommended instrument; non-transferable and without banker's acceptance in favour of the beneficiary to mitigate pre-shipment risk. The SL must designate a single clearing account at Banco Santander or CaixaBank for routing all outbound payments and maintaining a clean audit trail of the 60-day payment cycle.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla EUR/USD FX Forwards (deliverable, tenor up to 12 months) transacted under an ISDA or Spanish Bank Master Agreement with the onshore Tier 1 bank

NDF (Non-Deliverable Forwards) — permissible under Spanish law for settlement only in exotic non-convertible currencies, but not applicable for EUR/USD; availability limited to Banco de España licensed credit institutions
Cross-currency basis swaps (EUR/USD) for interest-rate and principal conversion of the working capital funding line
FX options (EUR call / USD put) to cap the cost of the lager imports where the SL carries a USD-denominated payable

Commodity price risk overlay is outside FX control scope, but the bank may offer a combination of EUR/USD forward plus a commodity forward quote on battery-grade lithium carbonate through its structuring desk under MiFID II conduct rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Depósito de Cuentas Anuales (annual filing of financial statements, directors' report and audit report if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end; calendar-year companies must file no later than 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers fines of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 depending on turnover. If accounts are not deposited within 18 months of the deadline, the company's registration sheet is closed, resulting in loss of good standing, inability to register subsequent corporate acts, and potential director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Impuesto sobre Sociedades — Modelo 200 (corporate income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT / Spanish State Tax Agency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months and 25 days after the tax year-end; calendar-year companies must file by 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharges: 5% if paid within 3 months; 10% for 3–6 months; 15% for 6–12 months; 20% after 12 months; plus late interest at 3.75% p.a. Accuracy-linked penalties range from 50% to 150% of the deficiency; non-filing can result in penalties of EUR 300 plus 0.5% of the net tax due.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración Anual de Titularidad Real (annual beneficial ownership declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) — filed together with the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 July for calendar-year companies when filed with the annual accounts; if a change in beneficial ownership occurs during the year, the declaration must be updated within 30 days of the shareholder transfer being recorded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is a serious infringement under Law 10/2010 on AML, attracting fines up to EUR 60,000; the registry may refuse subsequent filings until the UBO declaration is rectified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalización de Libros Obligatorios (legalisation / stamping of mandatory corporate books)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the financial year; calendar-year companies must legalise books by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalised books have no probative value in court and the company is subject to fines under Commercial Registry Regulations; continued non-compliance may be treated as a serious registry offence and affect the company's ability to file valid annual accounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required when the company meets at least two of the following thresholds at the balance sheet date for two consecutive financial years: (i) total assets exceed EUR 4,000,000; (ii) annual net turnover exceeds EUR 8,000,000; (iii) average number of employees exceeds 50. Permanently subject companies (credit institutions, insurance undertakings, listed entities, public-interest entities, and those in regulated sectors) are always audited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC) as approved by RD 1514/2007 and subsequent amendments; small and medium entities may use the simplified PGC for PYMEs. Consolidated financial statements must be prepared under EU-IFRS when the entity belongs to a group required to consolidate.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The directors must annually review and confirm the ultimate beneficial owners reflected in the company's records. The Declaración de Titularidad Real is submitted together with the annual accounts deposit to the Commercial Registry each calendar year. Any shareholding transfer that changes the UBO must be recorded in the Libro Registro de Socios and publicised by updated declaration filed at the Registry within 30 days of the transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Minute Book of General Meetings (Libro de Actas de la Junta General)
Register of Directors' Meeting Minutes (Libro de Actas de los Administradores)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard rate 25%; reduced rate 23% for SMEs with annual turnover ≤ €1 million; 100% first-year deduction for R&D expenditure; additional incentives for innovation, energy efficiency, and regional development

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 - Impuesto sobre Sociedades, mandatory electronic filing through AEAT Sede Electrónica
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days following the end of the tax year (fiscal year-end)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable net income before loss carryforwards and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Spanish tax resident SL must report worldwide income; non-resident shareholders file via withholding at source

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Retenciones e ingresos a cuenta
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding taxes and advance payments credited
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents claim treaty relief via TRC; dividends and royalties subject to 19% WHT unless reduced

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax liability after all adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents with Spanish-source income only; permanent establishment reporting required if applicable

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 100 euros per day (maximum 1,500 euros); non-filing: 3,000 euros plus 5% of undeclared tax; incorrect declaration: 100-200% surcharge on additional tax due

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders (reduced by applicable double tax treaties)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) from AEAT prior to dividend payment; submit beneficial ownership declaration, TRC application form, and supporting documentation via Sede Electrónica
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory rate (reduced to 0-10% under most treaties); Interest: 19% statutory rate (reduced to 0% under OECD-compliant treaties)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €1,000,000 local file threshold; €20,000,000 consolidated group revenue for master file obligation
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spanish Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to relevant activities; lithium carbonate trading requires adequate local substance, employees, and core income-generating activities to avoid recharacterization

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or overstatement of deductible expenses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty under Articles 305-309 Código Penal: 1-6 years imprisonment and fines equal to 50-200% of evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors face joint and several civil liability for tax debts, criminal prosecution, fines up to €600,000, and possible disqualification from corporate offices

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or maintaining Spanish SL solely for treaty shopping or profit shifting without economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties up to 100% of tax benefit obtained; criminal fraud charges if intent to defraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability for fraud, restitution of unjust enrichment, and potential imprisonment; AEAT may seek director disqualification and asset recovery

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain TP documentation or apply arm's length principle to intra-group transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties of 100-200% of tax adjustment; possible criminal sanctions for aggravated cases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for any resulting tax shortfalls; fines and disqualification risk under Spanish corporate governance rules

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct enhanced due diligence on cross-border lithium carbonate transactions or report suspicious activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million; criminal liability under Ley 10/2010 and AMLD5/6
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, imprisonment, and disqualification; joint liability for company fines and reputational damage
